dedupe_keys.name: community network map of us municipal fibre and broadband networks ilsr

description: The Community Network Map tracks the ways US local governments have invested in wired telecommunications networks and the state laws that discourage such approaches. Contents: 400 municipal networks serving more than 700 communities, from Chattanooga's large FTTH network to small towns connecting a few local businesses, with additive filters for network characteristics; networks serving more than one community are shown connected by a web. More than 200 communities are served by a publicly owned network that blankets the whole city with fibre, and the map is being expanded to Indigenously owned networks and telephone and electric cooperatives. Producer: the Institute for Local Self-Reliance. Coverage: the United States, at community level. Access: an interactive public map, with a weekly email list for updates; no download link was seen. Licence and cost: free; no licence stated. Caveats: the map records ownership models and deployment types, not route geometry or speeds, and inclusion depends on the compilers' research. Simulation uses: it identifies publicly owned networks and state constraints for broadband deployment, ownership and resilience scenarios. Related record: NaNDA broadband internet by tract (data-nanda-broadband-internet-by-tract), which gives availability measures.
